text:
mira: Two-song, two-mood challenge — one track for a drizzly morning commute, one for a late-night reading session. Bonus: recommend a short book (<300 pages) that vibes with the late-night pick. I'll go first: morning = King Krule - 'Easy Easy' (cozy grimy energy), late-night read = Nick Drake - 'Pink Moon' on repeat, book = 'Stoner' by John Williams (quiet, dense, ~250p).
jon: Love this. Morning = Khruangbin - 'White Gloves' (easy groove), late-night = Sufjan Stevens - 'Death With Dignity', book = 'The Sense of an Ending' (short, unsettling). :books::coffee:
samir: Morning = Otis Redding - 'Sittin' On The Dock of the Bay' (slow and warm), late-night = Radiohead - 'Life in a Glasshouse', book = 'The Vegetarian' (short but sticky).
eva: haha @mira your Nick Drake + Stoner combo is chef's kiss. My pair: morning = Nile Rodgers & CHIC - 'Everybody Dance', late-night = Nils Frahm - 'Says', book = 'Lab Girl' (memories-y, not too long). :sparkles:
olivia: Quick one — morning = Alan Walker - 'Heading Home' (nostalgic pop), late-night = Agnes Obel - 'Riverside', book = 'The Ocean at the End of the Lane' (magical and compact).
book-bot: suggestion: If you liked 'Stoner', consider 'The Mezzanine' by Nicholson Baker (~130 pages) — micro-obsessions pair well with quiet late-night piano.
mira: adding a tiny poll — who'd actually make a playlist out of these? :raised_hands: 1) me 2) maybe 3) never
jon: 1

mira: awesome — gonna stitch these into a 30-min 'rain-to-night' mix and drop it in #playlists later. thanks y'all :)
